newsitem.title: UK: Burnfield advisers say accept Fairey offer.
newsitem.headline: Burnfield advisers say accept Fairey offer.

text.p: Electronics and engineering manufacturer Fairey Plc said on Monday that financial advisers to its takeover target Burnfield Plc had recommended its increased offer for the systems manufacturer.

In a statement, Fairey explained that Burnfield itself was prevented from recommending the offer to shareholders by under- takings it has given in a separate proposal to buy Ling Dynamic Systems (LDS). These plans were stalled last week when Burnfield suspended an extraordinary meeting meant to approve that buy.
Fairey said in a statement that Burnfield's advisers Merrill Lynch, not so bound, consider its offer "fair and reasonable".
Fairey posted its increased offer, which proposes 25 of its shares for every 92 of Burnfield's, on Friday.

"Merrill Lynch International...has advised the board of Burnfield that, taking into account the commercial assessments of the directors of Burnfield, it considers the terms of the increased offer to be fair and reasonable," Fairey said.
Fairey added it was urging Burnfield shareholders to accept the offer as soon as possible, and before a deadline of 1500 GMT on January 17.
One condition of the Fairey offer is that Burnfield drops its proposed LDS acquisition and an associated rights issue.
Burnfield said that it had postponed the egm on LDS until January 23 in order to allow its shareholders time to consider Fairey's proposals.
In addition to the share-based offer, Burnfield shareholders have also been assured of a net dividend of 2.2 pence each which would represent Burnfield's final dividend for 1996.
